check.reason: The headline says Oura 'Delays IPO', which is not in the real story and is presented as fact. That breaks the rule against inventing facts and misstating what the story is about. The headline is also written like a plausible straight news item, so the satire is weak. The $625 million and the acquisition are accurate, and the take targets the company, not patients. The 'readiness score is 62' line is an invented specific number and should be changed to a non-numeric phrase. Fix: remove the IPO claim, e.g. 'Smart Ring Maker Spends $625 Million to Answer the Questions Its Ring Raised', and drop the specific score.

pick.title: Oura to acquire Counsel Health for $625 million, placing a big bet on AI care
pick.headline: Smart Ring Maker Delays IPO, Spends $625 Million on Clinical AI
pick.take: After years of telling patients their readiness score is 62, the ring company is moving into care itself. The business plan is a finger-worn device that generates concerns and an AI that responds to them. The physician who eventually reviews all this will, as usual, not be on the cap table.
